title: Deploying GenAI Applications
summary: A model is only useful when others can access it. You wrap your LLM logic in a FastAPI backend, build a UI with Streamlit or Gradio, containerize with Docker, and deploy to the cloud. These full-stack deployment skills turn prototypes into real produ
content:
# Deploying GenAI Applications ##### The demo that only ran on one laptop A three-person team in Indore built an excellent RAG assistant for a client's compliance documents. Good retrieval, reranking, citations, guardrails — everything from the last six days, done properly. The client asked for a demo on a Tuesday. The engineer who built it was in Chennai for a wedding. Nobody else could run it. His `requirements.txt` was stale. His `.env` was on his machine. The Chroma index was in a local folder that had never been committed. The one teammate who tried spent four hours fighting a `chromadb` version conflict and gave up. The demo was rescheduled by nine days. The client took a meeting with a competitor in the interim. **A model that runs on one laptop has no value.** Deployment is not the boring part after the interesting work — it is the step that converts your work into something that exists for other people. Today you make that happen. ##### The deployment stack ```mermaid flowchart TD A["User's browser"] --> B["Gradio / Streamlit UI"] B -->|HTTP| C["FastAPI backend"] C --> D["RAG pipeline
retrieve → rerank → generate"] D --> E[("Vector DB
persisted volume")] D --> F["LLM API"] C --> G["Guardrails
Day 40"] subgraph DOCKER["Docker container"] B C D G end DOCKER --> H["Cloud host
Render / Cloud Run / HF Spaces"] I["Secrets from
environment"] -.-> C ``` Four layers: an API that exposes your logic, a UI that people can use, a container that makes it reproducible, and a host that gives it a URL. ##### FastAPI for LLM backends FastAPI is the standard choice: async by default (important, because LLM calls are I/O-bound and slow), automatic OpenAPI docs, and Pydantic validation built in. ```python # app/main.py import os, time, uuid, logging from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from typing import Literal from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from .rag import RAGPipeline from .guardrails import moderate, detect_injection logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='{"ts":"%(asctime)s","lvl":"%(levelname)s","msg":%(message)s}') logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) state: dict = {} @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app: FastAPI): logger.info('"loading pipeline"') state["rag"] = RAGPipeline( db_path=os.environ.get("VECTOR_DB_PATH", "/data/chroma"), model=os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"), ) yield state.clear() app = FastAPI( title="Compliance RAG Assistant", version=os.environ.get("APP_VERSION", "0.1.0"), lifespan=lifespan, ) app.add_middleware( CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=os.environ.get("ALLOWED_ORIGINS", "*").split(","), allow_methods=["GET", "POST"], allow_headers=["*"], ) class QueryRequest(BaseModel): question: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=1000) top_k: int = Field(5, ge=1, le=20) doc_type: Literal["policy", "circular", "any"] = "any" class Source(BaseModel): source: str page: int | None = None score: float class QueryResponse(BaseModel): request_id: str answer: str sources: list[Source] latency_ms: float tokens_used: int def verify_key(x_api_key: str = Header(None)): expected = os.environ.get("APP_API_KEY") if expected and x_api_key != expected: raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key") @app.get("/health") async def health(): return {"status": "ok", "version": app.version, "model": os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL")} @app.post("/query", response_model=QueryResponse, dependencies=[Depends(verify_key)]) async def query(req: QueryRequest): rid = str(uuid.uuid4()) t0 = time.perf_counter() if detect_injection(req.question)["suspicious"]: logger.warning('"blocked injection: %s"', rid) raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Request rejected") try: result = await state["rag"].answer_async( req.question, k=req.top_k, doc_type=req.doc_type ) except Exception: logger.exception('"pipeline failure %s"', rid) raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Internal error") latency = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000 logger.info('"query","rid":"%s","latency_ms":%.1f,"tokens":%d', rid, latency, result["tokens"]) return QueryResponse( request_id=rid, answer=result["answer"], sources=result["sources"], latency_ms=round(latency, 1), tokens_used=result["tokens"], ) ``` **Four production details in there.** The pipeline loads **once at startup** via `lifespan`, not per request — loading an embedding model on every call would add seconds. Pydantic validates at the boundary, so malformed input returns 422 rather than a traceback. Every request gets an ID that appears in the logs. And errors are logged with full detail but return a generic message, because stack traces leak internal structure. ##### Streaming endpoints Day 31 established that streaming is a UX decision. Here it is at the HTTP layer, using Server-Sent Events. ```python import json from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse @app.post("/query/stream", dependencies=[Depends(verify_key)]) async def query_stream(req: QueryRequest): rid = str(uuid.uuid4()) async def event_generator(): try: # Send sources first so the UI can render citations immediately chunks = await state["rag"].retrieve_async(req.question, k=req.top_k) yield f"data: {json.dumps({'type': 'sources', 'request_id': rid, 'sources': [c['meta'] for c in chunks]})}\n\n" async for token in state["rag"].generate_stream(req.question, chunks): yield f"data: {json.dumps({'type': 'token', 'content': token})}\n\n" yield f"data: {json.dumps({'type': 'done', 'request_id': rid})}\n\n" except Exception as exc: logger.exception('"stream failure %s"', rid) yield f"data: {json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'message': 'Generation failed'})}\n\n" return StreamingResponse( event_generator(), media_type="text/event-stream", headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"}, # disable nginx buffering ) ``` **`X-Accel-Buffering: no` is the header that saves an afternoon.** Without it, nginx and several cloud proxies buffer the entire response and deliver it at once, so streaming works locally and mysteriously does not in production. Sending sources before tokens is a deliberate UX choice: citations appear instantly while the answer types out. ##### Gradio and Streamlit Both let you build a usable UI in Python without touching JavaScript. | | Gradio | Streamlit | |---|---|---| | Best for | ML demos, chat interfaces | Data apps, dashboards | | Chat components | Excellent, built-in | Good (`st.chat_message`) | | Free hosting | HF Spaces | Streamlit Community Cloud | | Streaming | Native via generators | Via `st.write_stream` | | API generated | Yes, automatically | No | ```python # ui/app.py — Gradio import os, json, requests, gradio as gr API_URL = os.environ.get("API_URL", "http://localhost:8000") API_KEY = os.environ.get("APP_API_KEY", "") def respond(message, history, top_k, doc_type): """Streams the answer; yields progressively longer strings.""" try: r = requests.post( f"{API_URL}/query/stream", json={"question": message, "top_k": int(top_k), "doc_type": doc_type}, headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY}, stream=True, timeout=90, ) r.raise_for_status() answer, sources = "", [] for line in r.iter_lines(): if not line or not line.startswith(b"data: "): continue event = json.loads(line[6:]) if event["type"] == "sources": sources = event["sources"] elif event["type"] == "token": answer += event["content"] yield answer elif event["type"] == "error": yield f"⚠️ {event['message']}" return if sources: cites = "\n".join( f"- `{s['source']}` p.{s.get('page', '?')}" for s in sources) yield f"{answer}\n\n---\n**Sources**\n{cites}" except requests.Timeout: yield "⚠️ The request timed out. Please try again." except Exception as exc: yield f"⚠️ Could not reach the service: {exc}" with gr.Blocks(title="Compliance Assistant", theme=gr.themes.Soft()) as demo: gr.Markdown("## Compliance Assistant\nAsk about policies. Every answer is cited.") with gr.Accordion("Settings", open=False): top_k = gr.Slider(1, 15, value=5, step=1, label="Chunks to retrieve") doc_type = gr.Radio(["any", "policy", "circular"], value="any", label="Document type") gr.ChatInterface( fn=respond, additional_inputs=[top_k, doc_type], examples=["What is the notice period for terminating the MSA?", "What is the room rent sub-limit?"], type="messages", ) if __name__ == "__main__": demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=7860) ``` **Handle errors in the UI.** A timeout that surfaces as a Python traceback in the browser is the difference between a prototype and a product, and it costs four lines. ##### Containerisation Docker is what solves the Indore problem. The container carries the Python version, every dependency, and the system libraries. ```dockerfile # Dockerfile FROM python:3.11-slim AS base ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \ PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \ PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 WORKDIR /app RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ build-essential curl \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # Copy requirements FIRST so this layer caches across code changes COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY app/ ./app/ COPY ui/ ./ui/ RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser \ && mkdir -p /data && chown -R appuser /app /data USER appuser VOLUME ["/data"] EXPOSE 8000 HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=40s --retries=3 \ CMD curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1 CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "2"] ``` **The requirements-before-code ordering matters.** Docker caches layers; putting `COPY requirements.txt` before `COPY app/` means a code change rebuilds in seconds instead of reinstalling every package. **Never run as root.** A compromised container running as root is a much worse day than one running as `appuser`. **`VOLUME ["/data"]`** is where your Chroma index lives, so it survives container restarts — the persistence lesson from Day 34, applied at the infrastructure layer. ```yaml # docker-compose.yml services: api: build: . ports: ["8000:8000"] env_file: .env volumes: ["./data:/data"] restart: unless-stopped ui: build: . command: python ui/app.py ports: ["7860:7860"] environment: - API_URL=http://api:8000 - APP_API_KEY=${APP_API_KEY} depends_on: [api] restart: unless-stopped ``` ```bash docker compose up --build ``` One command, and anyone on the team has the whole system running. **Pin your dependencies.** `chromadb==0.5.5`, not `chromadb`. The Indore team's four-hour version conflict was an unpinned requirement. ##### Secrets Day 31's rules, now at the deployment layer: ``` .env ← local only, gitignored, never committed .env.example ← committed, variable names with empty values ``` ```python # app/config.py import os from functools import lru_cache from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings class Settings(BaseSettings): openai_api_key: str app_api_key: str | None = None llm_model: str = "gpt-4o-mini" vector_db_path: str = "/data/chroma" allowed_origins: str = "*" log_level: str = "INFO" class Config: env_file = ".env" @lru_cache def get_settings() -> Settings: return Settings() # raises immediately if a required key is missing ``` **Failing at startup on a missing secret is a feature.** A container that boots and then 500s on the first user request is much worse than one that refuses to start with a clear error. In production, inject secrets through the platform: Render environment variables, Cloud Run secret references, or Kubernetes secrets. Never bake them into the image — anyone who can pull your image can read them. ##### Deploying to the cloud | Platform | Free tier | Best for | Watch out | |---|---|---|---| | **HF Spaces** | Yes, generous | Gradio demos, portfolio | Public by default | | **Render** | Yes, sleeps when idle | Full stack, easy Docker | Cold starts ~30s | | **Railway** | Trial credits | Quick Docker deploys | Credits run out | | **Cloud Run** | Generous free tier | Production, scales to zero | GCP setup complexity | | **Fly.io** | Small free tier | Low latency, global | Config learning curve | For a portfolio project, **Hugging Face Spaces** is the fastest path to a public URL: ```yaml # README.md frontmatter in your Space repo --- title: Compliance RAG Assistant emoji: 📋 sdk: docker app_port: 7860 --- ``` Push, and it builds and deploys automatically. Set secrets in the Space settings, never in the repo. For something more production-shaped, Cloud Run: ```bash gcloud run deploy compliance-rag \ --source . \ --region asia-south1 \ --allow-unauthenticated \ --memory 2Gi --cpu 2 \ --min-instances 0 --max-instances 5 \ --timeout 300 \ --set-secrets OPENAI_API_KEY=openai-key:latest ``` `--region asia-south1` is Mumbai — lower latency for Indian users and relevant to data-residency expectations under the DPDP Act. `--min-instances 0` means you pay nothing when idle, at the cost of cold starts; set it to 1 if latency matters more than cost. `--max-instances` is a cost ceiling, not just a capacity setting. ##### A deployment checklist - [ ] `/health` endpoint returning version and model - [ ] All secrets from environment; `.env` gitignored - [ ] Dependencies pinned to exact versions - [ ] Non-root container user - [ ] Vector index on a persistent volume - [ ] Structured JSON logging with request IDs - [ ] Timeouts on every external call - [ ] Rate limiting on public endpoints - [ ] CORS restricted to known origins - [ ] Errors return generic messages; details only in logs - [ ] Guardrails from Day 40 wired into the request path - [ ] README with setup, architecture, and a live URL ##### Common mistakes - **Loading the model per request** instead of at startup. - **Unpinned dependencies** — the four-hour version conflict. - **Secrets in the image** or in the repo. - **Running as root.** - **No persistent volume**, losing the index on every restart. - **Missing `X-Accel-Buffering: no`**, so streaming works locally and not in production. - **`allow_origins=["*"]`** in production with an authenticated API. - **No timeouts**, so one hung LLM call blocks a worker indefinitely. - **Returning stack traces to clients.** - **No health endpoint**, so orchestrators cannot tell whether you are alive. - **Building on your laptop's Python version** and discovering the container has a different one. - **No rate limiting**, letting one user exhaust your API budget. ##### Hands-on: get a public URL today Your practical task wraps your RAG app in FastAPI with streaming and connects a Gradio front end. Build the API first and test it with `curl` before writing any UI — separating the two layers is what lets you debug each independently. Then open `http://localhost:8000/docs` and use the auto-generated Swagger interface to exercise your endpoints; it is free and it catches schema mistakes immediately. The mini project deploys the containerised app to a free host with a public URL. Do the Docker step properly even though it feels like overhead: build locally, run `docker compose up`, and confirm it works in a fresh container *before* pushing anywhere. Debugging a build on a remote host is far slower. Then send the URL to someone who has never seen the project and watch them use it — you will find three UX problems in five minutes. The assignment is a deployment guide covering architecture, Dockerfile, and environment configuration. Write it for a colleague joining on Monday who has never seen the repo. Include the architecture diagram, a table of every environment variable with its purpose, exact commands to run locally and to deploy, and a troubleshooting section for the three things you got stuck on. That document is what would have saved the Indore team nine days. ##### Key takeaways - **A model that runs on one laptop has no value** — deployment is what converts your work into something other people can use. - **Load models at startup, not per request**, validate at the boundary with Pydantic, and give every request an ID that appears in your logs. - **Docker makes it reproducible**: pin dependencies exactly, copy requirements before code for layer caching, run as non-root, and mount your index on a persistent volume. - **Secrets come from the environment and the app fails fast if they are missing** — never bake them into an image or commit them. - **Ship the checklist, not just the code**: health endpoint, timeouts, rate limits, restricted CORS, generic error messages, and a README with a live URL.
